subject: Conversion to Tiered Commit Buckets & Throttle Safeguard
messages:
From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@olivetech.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — commit increase question

Hi Camila,

Quick question as we look at next quarter's commitment: we'd like to move away from a single flat monthly commit and instead adopt a tiered/bucketed commit model so we can smooth spikes across campaigns. Two specific asks: 1) can Redwood support bucketed monthly commitments (e.g., Base / Peak / Burst buckets) with predictable per-token rates per bucket, and 2) can we include an automatic throttle safeguard so we avoid surprise overages that would break our campaign budgets? Procurement also wants a short SOW and pricing summary to review.

Can you send a proposal (pricing + SOW stub) and any recommended guardrail thresholds based on your experience with other ad/retail customers?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Ellis
Head of Growth
OliveTech
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@olivetech.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — commit increase question

Hi Sam — great to hear from you, and thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can convert your flat commit to a tiered/bucketed model and include an automatic throttle/fallback mechanism.

I've attached a one-page proposal that outlines:
- Suggested bucket sizes (Base / Peak / Burst) calibrated to OliveTech's historical 6-month usage.
- Per-token rates per bucket and the overage protection options (throttle vs. soft overage with notification).
- Operational controls: per-route rate limits, per-project KV-cache retention, and automatic model fallback to a smaller variant if sustained burst usage hits the safety threshold.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben will send an initial pricing grid and recommended bucket thresholds.
2) I'll circulate a draft SOW for procurement to review.
3) Quick 30-min sync this week to align on burst sizing and billing terms.

Attaching: Redwood_Tiered_Buckets_Proposal_Jul2028.pdf (proposal) and SOW_OliveTech_TieredBuckets_v1.docx (SOW stub).

Do any of these times work? Wed 10:00–10:30 or Thu 14:00–14:30 PT.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@olivetech.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal prep — commit increase question

Camila / Sam — I ran the numbers against OliveTech's trailing 6 months (campaign + realtime inference). Here are the draft pricing buckets and recommended thresholds:

- Base bucket: 300M tokens / month — covers regular traffic — rate: $0.0008 / token
- Peak bucket: additional 150M tokens / month — for predictable seasonal lift — rate: $0.0006 / token
- Burst bucket: 50M tokens / month (consumable) — for unexpected spikes — rate: $0.0012 / token (consumable bucket)

Overage / throttle options (choose one):
- Soft overage: charge at burst rate but send daily alerts;
- Hard throttle: stop generation beyond burst bucket and return 429 with a friendly error + telemetry to your engineers;
- Auto-fallback: when burst sustained beyond 60s, automatically downgrade to a smaller model family with a tight latency SLO.

Recommendation: pick Soft overage + Auto-fallback as default; add Hard throttle as a safety switch procurement can flip.

I attached a sample pricing grid to the proposal. If you want we'd also add an SLA credit schedule tied to latency targets for the Base bucket.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Also please confirm whether data processed by Redwood (for inference) will be included in your SOC2 scope and whether the audit report can be uploaded to our secure portal.

Subject: Re: Renewal prep — SOW and billing questions

Hi — thanks for the details. Responses inline below and in the updated SOW (attached):

- Billing terms: We can support Net-30 default; Net-60 and Net-90 are available for enterprise agreements (we'll call this out in the SOW).
- Invoice layout: Burst bucket consumption will be a discrete invoice line ("Burst usage — tokens") so it is easy to track and allocate to campaign cost centers.
- Compliance: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II covers hosted inference; I have included a link in the SOW to the audit artefact and we can route the report to your secure portal.

Sam — once you confirm the bucket sizes above we will finalize the SOW and Ben will send the updated pricing table to lock in rates for a 12‑month term with a 10% one-time onboarding credit (pending internal approval).

Proposed short next step: sign-off from your procurement on the SOW + 30-min technical handoff with our infra team to confirm rate-limit headers and telemetry.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
